column2: Map of the 11 locations, colored by mean MODIS mid-greendown date 2001–2025. Northern sites peak ~Sep 28; Shenandoah is latest (~Oct 10).
Peak date in every year 2001–2025 (dots) with the location mean and 95% CI (black). Locations are ordered north to south. Year-to-year spread (~±4 d) is similar to the spread between locations.
Share of the total sum of squares in peak date explained by location (fixed site differences), year (weather shared across the Appalachians) and the remainder. Location F = 56.7, year F = 18.9.
Mean difference in peak date between every pair of locations, paired by year. Pairing removes the weather all sites share, so differences of ~1.5 d are detectable. Stars: Holm-adjusted significance.

Every candidate location descriptor, ranked by leave-one-location-out error when used alone to predict the site's mean peak date. Left: correlation with permutation significance. Right: out-of-sample MAE vs. the no-predictor benchmark (orange).

Mean peak date of each location against latitude, forest elevation, longitude, September normal temperature, northern-hardwood share and the climatological date mean temperature falls below 12 °C. n = 11; Shenandoah sits above every fit.

For thresholds 8–18 °C, the date each location's 2001–2025 climatological (15-day smoothed) mean temperature first falls below T, related to the location's mean peak date. Left: correlation. Right: leave-one-location-out error.
Correlation between location descriptors across the 11 sites. Latitude, temperature normals, species mix and thermal date form one block, so with n = 11 they cannot be separated statistically.

Coefficients of latitude, elevation and the 15 °C thermal date in nested models of the location mean. Elevation only matters once latitude is held fixed; both lose their effect once the thermal date enters (mediation through temperature).
Added-variable plots. Holding latitude fixed, higher sites peak later? The partial slopes are -1.55 d per degree latitude and -1.10 d per 100 m of forest elevation.

Leave-one-location-out error for predicting the typical peak of a location not used in fitting. Nested selection (search repeated inside every fold) gives the honest number for a model chosen from data.

Left: observed location mean vs. the value predicted from the date the site's climatological mean temperature falls below 15 °C. Right: held-out residuals with Cook's distance; Shenandoah is ~5 d later than its climate implies.
Correlation of yearly peak-date anomalies (2001–2025) for all 55 location pairs against distance. Exponential decay fit gives an e-folding distance of 948 km; Mantel permutation p = 0.0001.
Correlation of yearly peak-date anomalies between every pair of locations (north → south). Blocks show a northern group, a central Appalachian group and the southern Blue Ridge.

Sensitivity of each location's peak-date anomaly to six forecast-safe weather/phenology anomalies. Orange line and band: pooled slope and 95% CI. The F-test asks whether slopes differ between locations.

Interaction tests: weather anomaly × standardized location moderator, pooled over 275 location-years with year-clustered SE. Cells show z and unadjusted p; † marks tests surviving Holm correction for 30 tests.
Best eight single interactions (weather feature × location moderator) added to a provisional base δ model (tmax_pre60to31, precip_pre60, mid_greenup_p50). Base LOYO MAE 2.96 d vs climatology 3.34 d.
Median peak-date anomaly of forest pixels by 100 m elevation bin within each location (anomaly relative to the location-year median, so weather and the location mean are removed).

Per-location linear slope of pixel peak anomaly on elevation (d per 100 m), alone and controlling for northness and forest fraction, with 95% CIs from a block bootstrap over years. Right: the aspect effect.

Left: improvement of a two-piece (hinge) elevation model over a straight line for each candidate break, by region group. Right: slope below and above the best break with bootstrap CIs (break re-selected in every replicate).
Elevation effect estimated between locations (orange), within locations (blue) and from the September temperature sensitivity of μ times the standard lapse rate (gray).

Best break elevation per location with bootstrap range and the slope above it. Clear steep upper segments exist at Montpelier (>600 m) and Asheville (>1,200 m); elsewhere breaks are weak or sit at the search edge.

Each location's mean peak relative to the 11-site mean, split into the part predicted by its climate (date the climatological mean temperature falls below 15 °C) and the local residual. Climate explains the north–south pattern; Shenandoah (+4 d) and Roanoke (−3 d) carry the largest local effects.

Predicted typical MODIS peak date over latitude and median forest elevation from μ ~ lat + elev (n = 11), with the 95% confidence half-width. Use inside the sampled range (dots); add the within-location elevation rule for individual summits.
